summary: Flag-driven lock acquisition on a graphics/resource object (__stdcall, called by sub_557670 and sub_558310). No-op when a1 is null. When flag bit 4 of a2 is set, allocates a buffer lock via BufferLockAllocate(a1[7], a2, a1[11], a1[2]) and stores the result at a1[8]. When flag bit 8 of a2 is set, allocates a surface blit lock via SurfaceBlitLockWithFlagCheck(a1[9], a2, a1[12], a1[4]) and stores the result at a1[10]. The two branches are independent and may both execute for the same call.

local_names.a1: resource object carrying the buffer and surface lock state
local_names.a2: flag mask; bit 4 requests the buffer lock, bit 8 requests the surface blit lock

operations.description: If a1 is null the function is a no-op; otherwise evaluate the flag mask.
When (a2 & 4) != 0, perform the buffer lock allocation.
Call BufferLockAllocate(a1[7], a2, a1[11], a1[2]) using the stored buffer pointer, the flag mask, and the sizing/control fields at a1[11] and a1[2].
Store the BufferLockAllocate result into the buffer-lock field a1[8].
When (a2 & 8) != 0, perform the surface blit lock allocation.
Call SurfaceBlitLockWithFlagCheck(a1[9], a2, a1[12], a1[4]) using the stored surface pointer, the flag mask, and the control fields at a1[12] and a1[4].
Store the SurfaceBlitLockWithFlagCheck result into the surface-lock field a1[10].
Return from the void function; invoked by sub_557670 (00557670) and sub_558310 (00558310).

unresolved: The meaning of the flag bits (4 = buffer lock, 8 = surface blit lock) and of the other bits in a2 is not documented in this packet.
The owning object type and the relationship between the a1[2]/a1[4] control fields and the lock allocations is unidentified.
Whether the two lock paths are mutually exclusive in practice or expected to be requested together is unknown.
